 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 04, 2026, 15:25:49 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st ODI: Indian skipper Shubman Gill won the toss and opted to chase against New Zealand in the first of the five ODIs in Auckland on Wednesday. 
 With the spotlight firmly on the road to the 2027 ODI World Cup, India begin their five-match series against New Zealand at Eden Park on Wednesday, with the return of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to the 50-over format. 
 India will also be looking to turn around their modest ODI record in New Zealand, where their last victory came in February 2019. Since then, they have featured in two ODI series in the country, suffering 3-0 and 1-0 defeats, with two matches washed out during the latter tour. 
 India have struggled for consistency in the 50-over format since winning the Champions Trophy in early 2025. In the six ODI series they have played since, the Men in Blue have won three and lost three, with defeats against Australia, New Zealand and England. 
 The last time these two sides met in an ODI series, New Zealand came out on top 2-1. 
 "We are going to bowl first. (It is a) bit overcast, so any reductions, it's good to have a target on the board. Everyone is excited and prepared for the series. Conditions we get here are going to be a lot similar to the ones we are going to get in SA. Anshul, Aaqib, Gurnoor and Arshdeep are the pacers," Gill said during the toss. 
 "Conway is doing well. He is going to rest up and obviously not going to play today. So Seifert gets a chance, and like India, we also have four pacers," New Zealand skipper Mitchell Santner said. 
 Teams: 
 New Zealand (Playing XI): Tim Seifert, Will Young, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham(w), Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner(c), Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy, Blair Tickner. 
 India (Playing XI): Shubman Gill(c), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, KL Rahul(w), Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Arshdeep Singh. Commentary

 15:25 (IST) Nov 04 To the 'Windy Welly' we go - Righto, that's that from the series opener. The rain interruptions took some shine off the occasion, but India go back with all smiles, while New Zealand are left with plenty to ponder, particularly a batting display that buckled under pressure. Both teams now head to the capital city, Wellington, for the second ODI which is set to be played at the Hnry Stadium on Saturday, November 7th. The first ball is set to be bowled at 2 am GMT (7.30 am IST). Do make sure to be with us in advance for the buildup and all other updates. Until then, take care, ADIOS!
 15:20 (IST) Nov 04 The Indian captain - Shubman Gill says that he is pleased with their all-round effort, particularly praising the bowling and fielding displays. He feels Rohit Sharma's brilliant run-out changed the momentum of the game, while also acknowledging the threat posed by Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips, who had troubled India with their partnership during the series in India as well. Gill is delighted with the way the team came together and credits Anshul Kamboj and Gurnoor Brar for their impressive spells. He describes Kamboj as someone tailor-made for these conditions, given his ability to generate seam movement and remain effective with the old ball, while adding that Brar brings extra bounce and pace when there isn't much assistance from the surface. Gill also reflects on the challenges of adapting to the conditions following the rain interruptions, noting that the pitch became quicker and offered more seam movement after the rain. However, he feels they stuck to their natural game, with their batting making the revised target much easier to chase. Looking ahead to the Wellington game, Gill doesn't feel there are any major areas to address, stressing that consistency will be key and that replicating this performance will put them in a very good position.
 15:19 (IST) Nov 04 The captain of New Zealand - Mitchell Santner reflects on the defeat. On what went wrong, he admits that the batting didn't go to plan, saying the pitch bounced more and was quicker than expected at Eden Park. He concedes that New Zealand probably didn't adapt as well as they could have, noting that battling the extra bounce made batting difficult. He adds that the surface skidded on nicely after the rain, credits the fast bowlers for adjusting well, and says the side picked up valuable learnings late in the game that they can take into Wellington.

 15:18 (IST) Nov 04 PLAYER OF THE MATCH - Anshul Kamboj gets the award for his outstanding bowling display of 2/22. Kamboj says that the key was to hit consistent lines and lengths and not to see how the wicket was behaving. Mentions that the wobble seam was working well and that he was just using that. He states that he gets good bounce off the wicket and that it is all about hitting the right length and focusing on that.
 15:18 (IST) Nov 04 ... The post-match Presentation ...
 15:18 (IST) Nov 04 Short ball sinks the Kiwis - A lively pitch, a well-drilled bowling attack, and a batting lineup that never found an answer - that was the story of New Zealand's innings. India's seamers turned the short ball into a potent weapon, while their smart use of the ground's dimensions ensured every disciplined spell brought reward. Arshdeep led the way with four wickets, Brar claimed three, and Anshul Kamboj delivered a quiet masterclass, finishing with 2/22 in 10 overs, including two maidens. Against that, New Zealand’s top order never settled. Seifert, Mitchell and Phillips each flickered into life, but none of them turned the flicker into a flame, and the hosts kept stumbling their way into trouble. The scoreboard would have made grim reading if not for Blair Tickner and Jacob Duffy, who swung freely in a last-wicket stand of 39 and rescued a total that was still well below par.

 15:16 (IST) Nov 04 Another masterclass by the chase master - Remember the tweet that went viral after Kohli's historic night at the MCG, the one saying it's his world and the rest of us are just living in it? Virat Kohli walked out already switched on, a few hours before turning 38, and chose to celebrate by doing what he does best, hunting runs. What set this knock apart was the appetite more than the shots. Chases bring out a certain hunger in him, and it showed in a rapid fifty off just 35 balls. Virat and Gill couldn't stay till the end, but their 113-run stand had already done the damage, prising the game out of the Kiwis' hands. Although Jacob Duffy and Co. troubled the batters with the short-ball ploy, with Duffy finishing with a three-wicket haul, it was just not enough in the end.
 15:14 (IST) Nov 04 Rain trims the chase - Conditions weren't that easy to bat on as seen in the first innings and India lost Rohit Sharma in the very first over itself which put them under a bit of pressure. However, Gill built the house with Kohli as they negotiated the new-ball phase. The two rode the bounce well and kept finding runs here and there as the Kiwi seamers operated with the same template of hitting the ball hard into the pitch. Then the heavens had their say. A frustrating rain delay of a good hour and a half chopped the game down to 40 overs, and when the clouds came back for a second round, the chase shrank again to 32 overs, with a DLS target of 143.
 15:11 (IST) Nov 04 Men in Blue get the job done - It wasn't the smoothest of finishes, with wickets quickly falling in the closing stages, but India have nonetheless gone 1-0 up in the five-match ODI series. India's bowling attack did the heavy lifting in this game, keeping New Zealand so far behind that they were never seen in the rearview mirror, and by the time they mounted a late charge, it was simply too little, too late.

 429 More Updates Load More India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st ODI: India won the toss and elected to bowl in the first ODI against New Zealand here at Eden Park on Wednesday as the Men in Blue play a five-game ODI series for the first time since March 2019.
With the ODI World Cup in the fray, veterans Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma are back in the mix. But skipper Shubman Gill will be wary of his limited resources and will look to start with a win and take an early lead in the series, with the squad set to shuffle for the final two games.
New Zealand, too, found themselves dealing with a string of injury blows ahead of the series opener. While Mark Chapman and Rachin Ravindra continue to recover from their respective injuries, regular opener Devon Conway was ruled out the day before the game after colliding with Matt Henry during training.
Despite these setbacks, the hosts have a well-rounded unit, with Glenn Phillips coming off a record-breaking T20I series. The visitors, meanwhile, will be without two key starters, Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya, while Prasidh Krishna has also been ruled out with an injury. Hence, both teams have considered their respective playing XIs ahead of the first game.
Winning the toss, Indian captain Shubman Gill mentioned that the side was aware of the overcast conditions, and were going in with four fast bowlers and two all-rounders in Naman Dhir and Axar Patel.
“We'll bowl first, bit of overcast weather, and in case there's a reduction of overs, it's good to chase. The conditions here are going to be similar to SA (where the WC is happening) compared to some other places. We are going with Anshul, Auqib, Gurnoor, Arshdeep as the bowlers with Naman and Axar as the allrounders,” Gill said.
Meanwhile, Blackcaps skipper Mitchell Santner said, “We've got to go again on another good pitch. With the schedules, there's been a bit more rotation. Conway is doing well. He is going to rest up and obviously not going to play today. So Seifert gets a chance and like India, we also have four pacers.
